clue.text: Breaking law taking bromine first during squabble

indicators.note: first says the bromine symbol goes at the front, ahead of the reworked letters

parts.note: Br is the chemical symbol for bromine

indicators.note: breaking the word law smashes it so its three letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone flouting the law while handling a chemical in the middle of an argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Breaking' rearranges LAW to AWL; 'taking bromine first' puts BR ahead of it. 'during' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A brawl is a noisy fight or quarrel, a rough synonym for a squabble.

parts.note: buckets are containers for water
to hop is to spring or jump

explanation.surface: Containers leaping out of a shady business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A bucket shop is a dodgy firm, originally an unofficial stockbroker or a cut-price travel agent.

clue.text: Overbearing for a bishop to go up to a group of conservationists

parts.note: RR, Right Reverend, is the title of a bishop

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word go is read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written before being turned
NT is the National Trust, the British body that conserves historic places

explanation.surface: A churchman is high-handed about joining a conservation group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' is the reversal signal in a down clue. The National Trust is a British charity that looks after historic houses and countryside. 'for' and 'to' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone arrogant is haughty and domineering, behaving with too much self-importance.

parts.note: William Laud was Archbishop of Canterbury under Charles I
being able means having enough power or capacity to do something

explanation.surface: An archbishop held enough authority to be praised.
explanation.walkthrough: William Laud was a 17th-century Archbishop of Canterbury, a name crosswords often use.
explanation.definitionFit: Laudable means worthy of praise, and commendable means deserving praise too.

indicators.note: included means the word for again sits inside the word for maps

parts.note: charts are maps, especially sea maps
re- is the prefix meaning again

explanation.surface: Someone redrawing the maps to take in a city in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'included' is the container signal; 'again' is easy to miss as a piece, since it reads as part of the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Chartres is a cathedral city southwest of Paris.

clue.text: Restraint at edge of pavement, say

indicators.note: say means the word for the edge of a pavement is spoken, giving a different spelling

parts.note: the kerb is the raised stone edge of a pavement

explanation.surface: Something holding things back at the side of a road.
explanation.walkthrough: KERB is the British spelling for the edge of a pavement; said out loud it matches the word for a check or limit.
explanation.definitionFit: A curb is a check or limit placed on something, as in a curb on spending.

indicators.note: composure is read as composing, putting the letters of regain together in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone getting a grip on themselves while visiting Canada.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composure' rearranges the letters of REGAIN; the definition is the place's location rather than its name.
explanation.definitionFit: Regina is the capital of Saskatchewan, a province of Canada.

parts.note: a second cup of tea poured into an emptied cup, one example of a top-up

explanation.definitionFit: A refill is a further helping poured into an empty cup or glass, and a second cup of tea is one example.
To shun is to keep away from someone; it is also the shortened parade-ground order for standing to attention.
Round as an adjective means ring-shaped, and a printed leaflet sent to many people is also called by this name.

clue.text: South American girl taken in by baron

indicators.note: taken in by means the girl's name is held inside the letters for baron

parts.note: Bn is the standard abbreviation for baron
Olivia is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A young woman deceived by an aristocrat on another continent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken in by' looks like 'fooled', but here it is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from Bolivia, a country in South America, is a native of that continent.

clue.text: Become a leader perhaps after being a follower

definitions.text: Become a leader perhaps after being a follower

parts.words: Become a leader perhaps after being a follower
parts.note: a car or runner who was behind moves past another and so goes ahead, as in a race

explanation.walkthrough: 'leader' and 'follower' look like people in charge and their supporters, but they are positions in a race or traffic.
explanation.definitionFit: To overtake is to pass a vehicle or runner that was ahead, moving from behind into front position.

clue.text: Glen and Dan coming from the country

indicators.note: coming from says the letters of the two names are reworked to give a new word

explanation.surface: Two men named Glen and Dan who hail from the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming from' rearranges the seven letters of GLEN and DAN; 'and' is only a link joining the two names.
explanation.definitionFit: England is one of the nations of the United Kingdom, a country in its own right.

parts.note: deb is the short form of debutante, a young socialite
a programme being transmitted is on air

explanation.surface: A society girl is briefly on radio, looking breezy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' says the debutante is cut to DEB.
explanation.definitionFit: Debonair describes a confident, charming and cheerful manner, close to light-hearted.

parts.note: the eyeball is a spherical organ, so something round
Ed is a short form of the name Edgar

explanation.surface: A man called Edgar was faced with some circular object.
explanation.definitionFit: To eyeball someone is to stare them down, facing them head-on.

clue.text: Found out it had been settled

explanation.surface: Someone discovered that a matter had already been resolved.
explanation.definitionFit: Determined means discovered by investigation, and also decided or fixed, as in a matter that has been resolved.

clue.text: This strike is not very sportsmanlike

definitions.text: This strike is not very sportsmanlike

parts.words: This strike is not very sportsmanlike
parts.note: a punch below the waistband is illegal in boxing, and the phrase also means any unfair tactic

explanation.walkthrough: A cryptic definition: the boxing foul and its everyday sense of an unfair attack.
explanation.definitionFit: In boxing a blow beneath the waistband is a foul, so the phrase names an unfair, unsporting attack.

clue.text: Happening seven times a week as usual

explanation.surface: Something that happens every day of the week, as normal.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done daily occurs on every one of the week's seven days, and the word also means ordinary or commonplace.

clue.text: Hesitate to cut out the written school task

indicators.note: to here means applied to, so the hesitation sound is set into the word for cut out

parts.note: to excise is to remove by cutting
er is the sound of someone hesitating

explanation.surface: A pupil wavering over whether to remove the written homework.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a loose container signal, read as 'applied to'; 'the' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece of written work set for practice at school is called an exercise.

clue.text: Book not likely to appeal to the hardened reader?

definitions.text: Book not likely to appeal to the hardened reader?

parts.words: Book not likely to appeal to the hardened reader?
parts.note: a hardened reader sounds like a seasoned bookworm but is one who prefers stiff covers, so a soft-covered book would not suit

explanation.walkthrough: 'hardened' looks like 'habitual', but it means someone who likes hardback books, so the book has soft covers.
explanation.definitionFit: A softcover book is the opposite of a hardback, so it would not appeal to someone who wants hard covers.

indicators.note: tucked into means the letter for one is slipped inside the word for pie

parts.note: a pizza is an Italian open pie
a means one, as in a dog

explanation.surface: Someone tucking into a pie in a square.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tucked into' looks like eating, but it puts A inside PIZZA, after the I.
explanation.definitionFit: A piazza is a public square, especially in an Italian town.

clue.text: Rex in pursuit of piece of timber

parts.note: R stands for Rex, Latin for king
to be after something is to be chasing it

explanation.surface: A dog called Rex chasing a piece of wood.
explanation.definitionFit: A rafter is one of the sloping beams of wood that hold up a roof.

indicators.note: suspect as an adjective means dubious, so the letters of a murder are unreliable and rearranged

explanation.surface: A suspect in a murder case is attending a court hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suspect' rearranges the seven letters of A MURDER; 'hearing' looks like a court session but means the sense of hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: The tympanic membrane in the ear vibrates with sound, an essential component of hearing.

indicators.note: round means the letters of darts off are turned about and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone throwing darts and touring a town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' rearranges the eight letters of DARTS OFF.
explanation.definitionFit: Stafford is the county town of Staffordshire in the English Midlands.

parts.note: one word means both a small error and a woman's underskirt, so a garment that is a mistake

explanation.definitionFit: A slip is a minor mistake and also a light underskirt or petticoat.
A short is a small strong drink of spirits, and a dram is also a small unit of fluid or weight.

clue.text: Roderick included a token, something that can be seen along the way

definitions.text: something that can be seen along the way

indicators.note: included means the letter a goes inside the short name

parts.note: Rod is a short form of the name Roderick
a sign is a token or symbol of something

explanation.surface: Roderick added a voucher to something he spotted on his travels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'included' is the container signal; the long definition is a roundabout way of describing roadside furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: A board giving directions or warnings stands at the roadside for travellers to read.

clue.text: Space to do some acting where children can be found

parts.note: to play is to act a part on stage
room means space, as in room to move

explanation.surface: A stage or rehearsal area where kids are found.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces come in the opposite order from the clue: 'Space to do some acting' gives ROOM to PLAY, written PLAY then ROOM.
explanation.definitionFit: A playroom is a room set aside for youngsters to play in.

indicators.note: leader's points to the first letter of youth
appalling means shocking, so the letters of idle are badly jumbled

explanation.surface: A lazy youth club leader shamefully gives up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader's' gives Y, the first letter of 'Youth'; 'appalling' rearranges IDLE to IELD.
explanation.definitionFit: To yield is to give way or hand over, as in giving up to an enemy.
